source.title: Astrocyte-neuron lactate transport is required for long-term memory formation

contexts.correctionCheck: Main publication metadata and available indexed records checked. No formal correction resolving the listed source inconsistencies was identified; correction and replication surveillance is incomplete.
contexts.finding: MCT4 and MCT2 knockdowns impaired long-term retention. L-lactate rescued the MCT4 condition; neither lactate nor equicaloric glucose rescued MCT2 knockdown.
limitations: Bilateral hippocampal antisense injections reduce the named transporter in tissue. They are not genetically restricted to a cell class. Astrocytic MCT4 and neuronal MCT2 attribution uses expression evidence; direct cell-to-cell lactate flux was not measured in these behavioral assays.

ODNs were injected 1 h before training; rescue L-lactate (100 nmol) or equicaloric glucose (50 nmol) was injected 15 min before training. Retention was tested at 24 h and 7 days, with 1 h short-term testing in a separate MCT2 assay.

The behavioral endpoint is inhibitory-avoidance entry latency. Supplementary animal, surgical and task procedures and Tables S4-S5 remain unread: age, sex, shock protocol and exact group statistics are not independently established here.

Figure 6 and the MCT2 Results report no lactate rescue; a Discussion sentence inconsistently lists MCT2 among rescued knockdowns. Other Results sentences pair significant impairment with p > 0.05. No numerical inference is derived from those inconsistent passages.

Rescue does not uniquely establish lactate as an exclusive energy substrate; redox, signaling and other metabolic explanations remain possible. The failed equicaloric glucose rescue is dose- and protocol-specific, not proof that glucose can never support retention.

contexts.finding: Deprived preparations had more CC1-positive oligodendrocytes, shorter internodes and slower, broader compound action potentials. Myelin-specific mediation was not isolated.
limitations: Both sexes were used. Long-term eyelid closure starts around P15 and ends at P32. Deprivation changes sensory experience during development; it is not a selective manipulation of myelin, nor elimination of all retinal activity.

CC1 cell counts, NG2-CreERT2/tau-mGFP internodes after P19 tamoxifen, and isolated optic-nerve compound action potentials use distinct assay preparations. They cannot be collapsed into measurements of one axon or a directly identified mediator.
Conduction velocity is nerve length divided by stimulus-to-CAP-peak latency at room temperature. CAP width describes a population waveform, not an identified single-axon speed or information code.

The main text and Figure 3 caption differ on the deprived internode median; Figure 7 repeats Figure 3 group labels, medians and sample counts despite a separate genetic assay. Figure 2 text/caption swap myelinated-axon percentages, and the reported conduction percentage does not directly match the caption means. Exact quantitative calibration remains unadmitted.

Internodes and axons are nested within mice. Raw measurements, animal-clustered uncertainty and plotted values have not been independently reproduced. Ultrastructural and paired-pulse nulls do not prove full equivalence.

contexts.finding: Selected microglial or purinergic perturbations altered neural readouts, adenosine assays and seizure susceptibility. A1 agonist rescue depended on the genetic preparation.
limitations: Adult seizure cohorts have conflicting descriptions: Animals gives 8-16 weeks for pharmacological experiments, while Seizure Induction gives 14-20 weeks for all seizure experiments. No exact age is selected from this conflict. Genetic cohorts generally include both sexes; pharmacological seizure cohorts are male.

These are distinct genetic preparations. Cx3cr1-CreERT2 targets a lineage rather than proving absolute microglia specificity; P2ry12 deletion is whole-animal, and Drd1a-Cre ligand/receptor deletions are developmental. Cre-negative littermates are the stated default controls.

Neonatal P5-P7 cultures and adult in vivo preparations remain separate. Figure 4c is extracellular striatal dialysate under isoflurane; Figure 4h is a tissue-homogenate fluorescence assay after D1 agonist.

Cortical bouton imaging and striatal calcium imaging are different preparations. The cortical caption says intraperitoneal CNO/clopidogrel while its Methods says intravenous CNO. The neuronal-imaging virus volume and the A1-antagonist dose units also contain unresolved inconsistencies.

Cell and process counts do not replace independent mice. Calcium magnitude and rate-interaction nulls, receptor-specific rescue failures and challenge-specific nulls constrain generalization. Code, raw imaging and all supplementary datasets have not been independently replayed.

Published results and source-table checks are not an independent biological replication. Behavioral stage IV-V seizures are an induced challenge endpoint, not a universal measure of neural stability or a human treatment result.

source.title: Rapid formation and selective stabilization of synapses for enduring motor memories — Supplementary Information

contexts.correctionCheck: PMC and publisher metadata and exact-DOI notice searches checked on 13 September 2026; no resolving correction identified. This is not exhaustive notice surveillance. Online publication 29 November 2009; issue date 17 December 2009.
contexts.finding: Novel motor training is accompanied by increased formation and elimination in selected cortical dendrites, and initially new spines are preferentially retained. The results constrain experience-dependent remodeling without proving a unique memory substrate or a universal construction law.
limitations: YFP-H mice were one month old or older than four months. Superficial apical dendrites of layer V pyramidal neurons were imaged 10-100 micrometers below the cortical surface under ketamine-xylazine anesthesia; these are selected cortical compartments, not a whole-brain connectome.

Main scientific text, Methods Summary and Figures 1-4 are reviewed. All text of the 12-page publisher supplement, Figures S1-S5 and Table S1 are reviewed, including visual inspection. The separate full Methods file and movie were not obtained or read; precise task procedures, sex, allocation, blinding and exclusions remain unverified.

Dense labeling prevented tracing complete individual neurons. The supplementary estimate of 20-80 sampled cells per mouse is not an identified neuron census. The study total of 32079 spines in 209 mice does not make spines independent animals or mean that every spine was followed for 120 days.

Formation and elimination are interval-specific percentages relative to the initial spine count. New-spine survival uses the newly appearing subset instead. These denominators cannot be exchanged or converted into universal growth rates, absolute density or graph weights.

General controls were littermates with the same food restriction and similar handling, without shaping or training. Learning, task exposure and reward are not individually isolated. Animal-level image stacks, cohort assignments and analysis code were not obtained; published tests were not independently reproduced.

The Figure 1f first-session training group selected four mice with more than ten successes in thirty reaches. Figure 1g also plots animals with ten or fewer successes, so the correlation cohort is not this selected four-mouse group. Imaging occurred within one hour after the session, but the baseline was from the previous day; this interval does not timestamp each spine birth within an hour.

Behavioral curves, spine-turnover cohorts and follow-up cohorts have different animal counts. The survival design uses two classification images and a third follow-up at a selected interval; it is not one fully sampled trajectory through every plotted timepoint.

Figure 2c normalizes total spine number to the initial image. Both control and trained trajectories lie below their initial value by day 16. Convergence toward control levels is distinct from the abstract wording about return to the original level; no exact count setpoint or one-for-one replacement is demonstrated.

Spine morphology does not directly measure synaptic currents, presynaptic partner identity or memory content. The study does not selectively remove the retained spines to test memory necessity or uniquely assign different memories to disjoint synaptic sets.

Motor mapping was terminal in fourteen mice: five imaging regions lay within the forelimb map, six on its border and three outside but within 300 micrometers. The map was not followed longitudinally, and distance from its border does not identify a complete circuit or a construction geometry.

Named nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests. The long-duration activity controls had marked attrition: only two mice still reached more than twenty times daily at day eight and one at day sixteen. They do not support a well-powered universal exclusion of motor activity.

Spine-size analysis used head diameter divided by adjacent shaft diameter in 29 surviving spines; the cited supplementary paragraph does not supply its animal count. This selected morphological ratio is neither absolute spine volume nor measured synaptic strength.

Persistence to the reported approximately 120-day follow-up is finite. Training for sixteen days followed by the long untrained interval does not demonstrate permanence, a globally minimal circuit or a unique homeostatic construction law.

contexts.finding: Selected birth-labeled neurons acquire neuronal morphology and electrophysiological responses. Input integration is supported in this preparation; unbiased generation rates, mature output transmission and memory necessity are not tested.
limitations: Female C57BL/6 mice were four to five weeks old at housing allocation and received virus one week later. Birth labeling therefore starts at approximately five to six weeks, not uniformly in fully mature adults. Electrophysiology was four to eight weeks after injection and used runners only.

Retroviral GFP labels a selected dividing-cell population. Variable infection, neuronal GFP downregulation and faint cells prevent absolute neurogenesis-rate estimation. BrdU incorporation is a separate DNA-labeling assay; a 48-hour count is not a count of mature functional neurons.

Of 58 recorded GFP-positive cells, 13 from 13 mice had neuronal physiology; 45 were nonexcitable and not all individually identified. The 13/58 fraction is a selected recording yield, not an unbiased neuronal differentiation probability. Unlabeled comparison neurons were not birthdated.

Sample sizes vary by assay and parameter. Table 3 compares up to 13 labeled neurons and 27 unlabeled neurons from 23 mice; cell nesting is not a fully reconstructed animal-level analysis. Randomized housing allocation, blinding and a prospective sample-size calculation are not reported in the reviewed Methods.

Spontaneous postsynaptic responses were seen in six labeled neurons, and perforant-path-evoked responses in four. Selective transmitter blockade is not supplied for every input. The paired-pulse example does not establish a universal sign rule, and afferent input is not direct proof of output transmission to CA3.

Table 3 nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests. The membrane time constant differs, and capacitance is calculated from time constant/input resistance rather than measured as a direct morphological quantity.

The four-week and four-month morphology samples contain different cells. Eight cells are used per age for most measures, with five for four-month spine density; their animal distribution is not resolved. This is not longitudinal tracking of the same dendrite.

Running and standard housing have separate BrdU samples of five and four mice. Housing is a multicomponent exposure, not a selective learning manipulation. Normal adult neurogenesis does not thereby require training or tissue injury.

Main experimental text, Methods, Figures 1-5 captions and Tables 1-3 were read in the PMC author manuscript; Figures 3-5 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-identified data and the LabVIEW acquisition code were not obtained or replayed.

No behavioral memory test or selective newborn-neuron ablation is performed here. Cell birth labeling, neuronal markers, synaptic morphology, input responses and cognitive necessity are distinct claims.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher metadata, the author-lab PDF and publisher supplementary PDF, and exact DOI correction, erratum and retraction searches were checked on 14 September 2026. No notice resolving the stated dose, reporter or denominator conflicts was identified. This is not exhaustive correction surveillance.
contexts.finding: PV activation suppresses population cycle markers and PV inhibition increases them; tested SST/VIP manipulations retain nulls. Conditional gamma2 deletion changes early activation and later clone composition. Isolation retains an EdU difference under PV activation, while MCM2 housing contrasts are nonsignificant. Full feedback closure and exclusive mediation remain unresolved.
limitations: Adult mouse preparations use nestin-GFP, PV/SST/VIP-Cre and nestin-CreERT2;Z/EG lines with gamma2-floxed or control alleles. Sex and a complete group-specific animal manifest are not reported. Tamoxifen is a single 62 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose at 6-10 weeks. The Methods require at least four weeks after AAV surgery; schematic week labels do not supply exact ages for every animal.

Acute 300-micrometre slices were recorded at 32-34 degrees C, with RGL voltage clamp at -65 mV and 5 mM kynurenic acid. The internal solution is ambiguously printed as 135 mM CsCl gluconate. Clamp-current sign does not directly identify native membrane polarization, spiking or cell-cycle entry.

Main text, Online Methods and Supplementary Figure 1 print 200 mM for focal GABA/muscimol application; no micromolar substitution is made. Etomidate is 100 nM in the main text/Figure 1 but 10 micromolar in Methods. The etomidate dose remains unresolved, and pharmacological sensitivity does not establish receptor stoichiometry.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. AAV volume, delivered light power and a full opsin-negative illumination control are not reported. No-light sham comparisons include the effects of the complete light protocol.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. EdU incorporation and MCM2 expression are cycle-related endpoints, not counts of completed neuronal differentiation, integrated neurons or an instantaneous birth rate.

Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. Optogenetic counts are limited to one millimetre anterior and posterior to the injection. Densities per cubic millimetre and the MCM2-positive fraction have distinct denominators. Analyses are described as blinded; random assignment, raw unit records and multiplicity-adjusted tests are not supplied.

At two and seven days after induction, one GFP-positive RGL is classified as a quiescent clone and two or more nuclei as an activated clone. These are fixed-tissue, spatially assigned clones using a referenced method, not live observations of every division or independently verified common ancestry. Supplementary Figure 2d plots one dentate gyrus per dot; hemispheres and clones cannot automatically be treated as independent animals.

Gamma2 immunostaining is shown in RGLs, but Supplementary Figure 2f electrophysiology tests GFP-positive neurons at thirty days, not RGLs. Its seven-of-ten cKO response pattern is not a measured RGL deletion efficiency. Recombination can persist in descendants, so later survival or differentiation may contribute to clone composition.

Thirty-day Figure 3f and Supplementary Figure 3e use incompletely reconciled clone denominators: the supplementary pie categories omit single-R and no-R classes. N includes intermediate progenitors or neurons, not exclusively mature neurons. Exact class percentages must not be pooled or converted to transition probabilities.

The population diazepam protocol is 5 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily for five days. The clonal drug comparison instead uses six daily doses after tamoxifen and analysis at seven days. Diazepam is systemic. Pairwise drug responses or nulls without a reported genotype-by-drug interaction do not isolate an exclusive cell-autonomous mediator.

Social isolation starts immediately after weaning and lasts at least six weeks before labeling. The two housing conditions are crossed with light versus sham; this is not a selective learning manipulation. PV activity and extracellular GABA are not measured as the intervening response to isolation in the same animals.

Figure 5c retains higher EdU-positive RGL density in isolated versus group-housed animals under PV light stimulation (reported P < 0.05). In that same housing comparison, MCM2-positive density and fraction are nonsignificant (P > 0.1). These endpoints do not support complete abolition of the isolation effect or equivalence; the light-treated group is also distinct from the untreated group-housed baseline.

Figure 4 population comparisons use three or four animals per condition; Figure 5c uses four. Reported Student t-tests do not provide an equivalence margin, complete unit manifest or a formal factorial interaction. SST/VIP nulls apply to the tested lines, protocols and readouts, not all possible interneuron functions.

No matched experiment follows physiological circuit demand through PV signaling, RGL division, newborn-neuron survival and functional integration to restoration of circuit output. Supplementary Figure 8 imports schematic connectivity proportions, not measured weights. A reported reconstruction covering over 200 RGLs is spatial coverage, not 200 verified functional contacts or a minimum carrier count. Movie legends were read; movie files and custom reconstruction code were not replayed.

All six main PDF pages, Figures 1-5, Online Methods and all nine supplementary PDF pages with Figures 1-8 and Movie 1-3 legends were reviewed. Raw animal-level data, microscopy, recordings, movie files and analysis code were not obtained or independently reproduced.

contexts.finding: PV activation suppresses population cycle markers and PV inhibition increases them; tested SST/VIP manipulations retain nulls. Conditional gamma2 deletion changes early activation and later clone composition. Isolation retains an EdU difference under PV activation, while MCM2 housing contrasts are nonsignificant. Full feedback closure and exclusive mediation remain unresolved.
limitations: Adult mouse preparations use nestin-GFP, PV/SST/VIP-Cre and nestin-CreERT2;Z/EG lines with gamma2-floxed or control alleles. Sex and a complete group-specific animal manifest are not reported. Tamoxifen is a single 62 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose at 6-10 weeks. The Methods require at least four weeks after AAV surgery; schematic week labels do not supply exact ages for every animal.

Acute 300-micrometre slices were recorded at 32-34 degrees C, with RGL voltage clamp at -65 mV and 5 mM kynurenic acid. The internal solution is ambiguously printed as 135 mM CsCl gluconate. Clamp-current sign does not directly identify native membrane polarization, spiking or cell-cycle entry.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. AAV volume, delivered light power and a full opsin-negative illumination control are not reported. No-light sham comparisons include the effects of the complete light protocol.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. EdU incorporation and MCM2 expression are cycle-related endpoints, not counts of completed neuronal differentiation, integrated neurons or an instantaneous birth rate.

Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. Optogenetic counts are limited to one millimetre anterior and posterior to the injection. Densities per cubic millimetre and the MCM2-positive fraction have distinct denominators. contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher metadata, the author-lab PDF and publisher supplementary PDF, and exact DOI correction, erratum and retraction searches were checked on 14 September 2026. No notice resolving the stated dose, reporter or denominator conflicts was identified. This is not exhaustive correction surveillance.
contexts.finding: PV activation suppresses population cycle markers and PV inhibition increases them; tested SST/VIP manipulations retain nulls. Conditional gamma2 deletion changes early activation and later clone composition. Isolation retains an EdU difference under PV activation, while MCM2 housing contrasts are nonsignificant. Full feedback closure and exclusive mediation remain unresolved.
limitations: Adult mouse preparations use nestin-GFP, PV/SST/VIP-Cre and nestin-CreERT2;Z/EG lines with gamma2-floxed or control alleles. Sex and a complete group-specific animal manifest are not reported. Tamoxifen is a single 62 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose at 6-10 weeks. The Methods require at least four weeks after AAV surgery; schematic week labels do not supply exact ages for every animal.

Acute 300-micrometre slices were recorded at 32-34 degrees C, with RGL voltage clamp at -65 mV and 5 mM kynurenic acid. The internal solution is ambiguously printed as 135 mM CsCl gluconate. Clamp-current sign does not directly identify native membrane polarization, spiking or cell-cycle entry.

Main text, Online Methods and Supplementary Figure 1 print 200 mM for focal GABA/muscimol application; no micromolar substitution is made. Etomidate is 100 nM in the main text/Figure 1 but 10 micromolar in Methods. The etomidate dose remains unresolved, and pharmacological sensitivity does not establish receptor stoichiometry.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. AAV volume, delivered light power and a full opsin-negative illumination control are not reported. No-light sham comparisons include the effects of the complete light protocol.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. EdU incorporation and MCM2 expression are cycle-related endpoints, not counts of completed neuronal differentiation, integrated neurons or an instantaneous birth rate.

Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. Optogenetic counts are limited to one millimetre anterior and posterior to the injection. Densities per cubic millimetre and the MCM2-positive fraction have distinct denominators. Analyses are described as blinded; random assignment, raw unit records and multiplicity-adjusted tests are not supplied.

At two and seven days after induction, one GFP-positive RGL is classified as a quiescent clone and two or more nuclei as an activated clone. These are fixed-tissue, spatially assigned clones using a referenced method, not live observations of every division or independently verified common ancestry. Supplementary Figure 2d plots one dentate gyrus per dot; hemispheres and clones cannot automatically be treated as independent animals.

Gamma2 immunostaining is shown in RGLs, but Supplementary Figure 2f electrophysiology tests GFP-positive neurons at thirty days, not RGLs. Its seven-of-ten cKO response pattern is not a measured RGL deletion efficiency. Recombination can persist in descendants, so later survival or differentiation may contribute to clone composition.

Thirty-day Figure 3f and Supplementary Figure 3e use incompletely reconciled clone denominators: the supplementary pie categories omit single-R and no-R classes. N includes intermediate progenitors or neurons, not exclusively mature neurons. Exact class percentages must not be pooled or converted to transition probabilities.

The population diazepam protocol is 5 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily for five days. The clonal drug comparison instead uses six daily doses after tamoxifen and analysis at seven days. Diazepam is systemic. Pairwise drug responses or nulls without a reported genotype-by-drug interaction do not isolate an exclusive cell-autonomous mediator.

Social isolation starts immediately after weaning and lasts at least six weeks before labeling. The two housing conditions are crossed with light versus sham; this is not a selective learning manipulation. PV activity and extracellular GABA are not measured as the intervening response to isolation in the same animals.

Figure 5c retains higher EdU-positive RGL density in isolated versus group-housed animals under PV light stimulation (reported P < 0.05). In that same housing comparison, MCM2-positive density and fraction are nonsignificant (P > 0.1). These endpoints do not support complete abolition of the isolation effect or equivalence; the light-treated group is also distinct from the untreated group-housed baseline.

Figure 4 population comparisons use three or four animals per condition; Figure 5c uses four. Reported Student t-tests do not provide an equivalence margin, complete unit manifest or a formal factorial interaction. SST/VIP nulls apply to the tested lines, protocols and readouts, not all possible interneuron functions.

No matched experiment follows physiological circuit demand through PV signaling, RGL division, newborn-neuron survival and functional integration to restoration of circuit output. Supplementary Figure 8 imports schematic connectivity proportions, not measured weights. A reported reconstruction covering over 200 RGLs is spatial coverage, not 200 verified functional contacts or a minimum carrier count. Movie legends were read; movie files and custom reconstruction code were not replayed.

All six main PDF pages, Figures 1-5, Online Methods and all nine supplementary PDF pages with Figures 1-8 and Movie 1-3 legends were reviewed. Raw animal-level data, microscopy, recordings, movie files and analysis code were not obtained or independently reproduced.

contexts.correctionCheck: PubMed/PMC metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked on 13 September 2026; no resolving notice identified. This is not exhaustive notice surveillance. Publication dated 11 April 2007.
contexts.finding: Selected peri-infarct samples show increased spine formation and altered morphology after photothrombosis. Recovery cohorts, optical readouts and spatial comparisons constrain injury-associated remodeling without proving behavioral restoration or a unique construction mechanism.
limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

The six-week density cohort reports five mice versus six controls but t(8)=1.43, P=0.09. The three-mouse near/far comparison reports t(3)=4.87, P<0.01 for formation and t(3)=1.92, P=0.08 for elimination. Sidedness and statistical units need resolution before numerical reproduction; these degrees of freedom do not establish an ordinary paired three-mouse test.

Orientation uses projected 15-30 micrometer segments, eighteen ten-degree bins, and three mice per group, with the infarct placed at a common reference position. Reported F(17,17) tests concern bin-distribution variance; bins are not independent mice and this is not an animal-level circular-statistical reconstruction.

The authors consider mechanical distortion during tissue loss and scar formation as well as growth and retraction. Projected dendrite-vessel alignment does not isolate shared guidance, establish physical contact or prove an optimal generative network geometry.

Texas Red dextran labels plasma. Capillary velocity in micrometers per second is distinct from volumetric perfusion; fluorescent vessel volume fraction is distinct from vessel number, connectivity and selectively demonstrated angiogenesis. The vascular cohort totals fourteen animals but per-timepoint assignments and segmentation routines remain unresolved.

The near/far spine comparison uses approximately 0.33 versus 1.65 millimeters from the infarct edge at two weeks. This is different from the orientation comparison of less than 250 versus 500-800 micrometers at six weeks. Restricted ipsilateral sampling does not establish absence of remodeling elsewhere.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

contexts.finding: Selected peri-infarct samples show increased spine formation and altered morphology after photothrombosis. Recovery cohorts, optical readouts and spatial comparisons constrain injury-associated remodeling without proving behavioral restoration or a unique construction mechanism.
limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

The six-week density cohort reports five mice versus six controls but t(8)=1.43, P=0.09. The three-mouse near/far comparison reports t(3)=4.87, P<0.01 for formation and t(3)=1.92, P=0.08 for elimination. Sidedness and statistical units need resolution before numerical reproduction; these degrees of freedom do not establish an ordinary paired three-mouse test.

Orientation uses projected 15-30 micrometer segments, eighteen ten-degree bins, and three mice per group, with the infarct placed at a common reference position. Reported F(17,17) tests concern bin-distribution variance; bins are not independent mice and this is not an animal-level circular-statistical reconstruction.

The authors consider mechanical distortion during tissue loss and scar formation as well as growth and retraction. Projected dendrite-vessel alignment does not isolate shared guidance, establish physical contact or prove an optimal generative network geometry.

Texas Red dextran labels plasma. Capillary velocity in micrometers per second is distinct from volumetric perfusion; fluorescent vessel volume fraction is distinct from vessel number, connectivity and selectively demonstrated angiogenesis. The vascular cohort totals fourteen animals but per-timepoint assignments and segmentation routines remain unresolved.

The near/far spine comparison uses approximately 0.33 versus 1.65 millimeters from the infarct edge at two weeks. This is different from the orientation comparison of less than 250 versus 500-800 micrometers at six weeks. Restricted ipsilateral sampling does not establish absence of remodeling elsewhere.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher/PMC metadata and exact-DOI correction searches checked on 13 September 2026; no resolving notice was identified. This is not exhaustive notice surveillance. Published online 11 July 2008; August 2008 issue.
contexts.finding: Labeled granule-cell populations produce functional output in selected slices. Direct versus indirect routes and cross-sectional morphology constrain circuit hypotheses without establishing behavior or a unique construction sequence.
limitations: Female C57BL/6 mice received retrovirus at five to seven weeks in Methods, versus six to seven weeks in Results, after three to seven days of running-wheel access. Anatomy at 17, 28 and 75 days after labeling and later slice physiology are separate samples, not uniform mature-adult stages.

Functional recording covered 43 slices from 34 mice at 8.6-20.6 weeks after labeling. Fourteen responding target cells came from 11 slices of nine mice at 13.4-20.4 weeks. Most recordings used 200 micromolar BaCl2 to increase excitability and all-trans retinal to assist ChR2; these are not ordinary in vivo signaling conditions.

Broad illumination activates a labeled population, not a single presynaptic neuron. CAG-ChR2-GFP and PGK-ChR2-IRES-RFP are different constructs. ChR2 expression changes with age and affects spike latency and capture; normal-looking morphology is not an equivalence test for absence of opsin effects.

Of 107 sampled targets, 76 were classified as interneurons, 16 as mossy cells, 11 as pyramidal cells and four remained unclassified. Fourteen responded: 11 interneurons, one mossy cell, one CA3 pyramidal cell and one unclassified cell. This selected yield is not a connection probability. Supplementary Table 1 classification samples have different denominators.

Kynurenic acid blocks upstream glutamatergic transmission in direct and indirect routes. Bicuculline sensitivity in two of five tested targets supports a polysynaptic inhibitory component, including the illustrated CA3 pyramidal response; it does not establish direct newborn-neuron excitation of that pyramidal cell.

Seven of 14 responses were judged probably monosynaptic from kinetics, latency and pharmacology; two were probably polysynaptic and five were not resolved. Latency is measured from light onset, includes opsin-dependent presynaptic spiking and is not a directly measured synaptic delay or unique hop count.

Bouton selection requires size above three axon diameters, connection to an axon and isolation for tracing. Cross-sectional confocal and electron-microscopic samples do not trace bouton replacement over time or provide an unbiased population geometry. Mouse allocation and the mapping between contact-census and profile-analysis denominators are incomplete.

CA3 contact censuses at 17, 28 and 75 days use eight, eleven and twelve boutons; the largest-section analyses use seven, nine and ten. Di-aminobenzidine labeling can obscure vesicles. The active-zone omnibus P=0.12 coexists with a significant reported post hoc contrast; this does not support uniform growth across all measures.

Main captions label some ANOVA statistics as t; the main Methods specify Fisher PLSD after significant ANOVA whereas Supplementary Table 1 uses Tukey comparisons. One brain was excluded for insufficient labeling. Complete animal allocation, blinding, sample-size planning and raw-recording manifests are unavailable.

Main experimental text, Methods, Figures 1-5 and the complete four-page supplement were read; all main and supplementary figures and Table 1 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-identified measurements and analysis code were not obtained or replayed.

The study measures morphology and output transmission, not behavior. Proposed recruitment of existing spines is a cross-sectional interpretation, not an observed minimal construction rule or proof of memory necessity.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

contexts.correctionCheck: The publisher correction dated 27 July 2004 was read and the corrected main PDF inspected. It does not resolve the stated sample-size, age and t/P conflicts and is not a retraction notice.
contexts.finding: Adult CpG site-16 patterns followed foster-care class. TSA altered several molecular readouts and the low-care group stress response, with site-specific and group-specific differences.
limitations: Long-Evans rat hippocampus is bulk tissue containing neurons and glia. High/low licking-grooming and arched-back nursing groups are selected extremes of continuous maternal behavior, not universal biological classes.

Cross-fostering changes a postnatal care environment. It does not isolate licking from nursing, nutrition or other maternal effects, directly manipulate an abstract neural state, or establish germline inheritance. Same-class foster controls are other mothers, not untouched biological-mother controls.

General adult-age statements conflict with assay-specific 90-day descriptions. ChIP figures report four animals/group but supplementary fixed-tissue methods specify six. GR protein Figure 5a reports five but Western methods specify six. Clones and technical blot replicates are not independent animals; litter dependence remains relevant.

Exon 1_7 is an alternative first exon of the rat glucocorticoid receptor gene. CpG site 16 at the 5-prime end of the NGFI-A binding region and site 17 at its 3-prime end have different outcomes. Bisulfite cytosine readouts, acetyl-H3K9-associated ChIP, NGFI-A ChIP, GR protein and plasma corticosterone are separate observables.

TSA infusion is a broad pharmacological intervention, not a locus-specific methylation edit or cell-specific neural manipulation. The restraint-stress cohort is separate from the GR-protein cohort. Parallel effects do not identify their causal mediation order.

The published Figure 2-associated t/P pairs (2.1/P<0.001 and 3.1/P<0.0001) are inconsistent with ordinary t tests; exact uncertainty is not reproduced. The 27 July 2004 publisher correction fixes labels, corticosterone units to micrograms/dL and bisulfite PCR annealing to 56 degrees C; the supplement retains conflicting text.

Individual animal source values and clone sequences are unavailable in the reviewed materials. Published findings are not an independent reproduction, and nonsignificant contrasts are not equivalence tests.

contexts.correctionCheck: Main publication metadata and available indexed records checked. No formal correction resolving the listed source inconsistencies was identified; correction and replication surveillance is incomplete.
contexts.finding: Relative activity perturbations changed engulfment preference. CR3/C3 loss reduced engulfment; CR3 loss increased projection overlap and structural synaptic puncta.
limitations: The preparation is the developing mouse retinogeniculate system. Engulfment is assayed at P5, segregation at P10/P30 and synaptic puncta at P32-35. Adult maintenance, immune surveillance, disease and all brain regions are not established by these developmental endpoints.

TTX/forskolin are intraocular pharmacological manipulations; CTB labeling follows 4-5 h later. Left-eye drug and right-eye vehicle inputs are compared within selected dLGN regions. Relative labeled-input engulfment is not a direct measurement of every synapse firing rate.

CR3/CD11b and C3 knockouts are developmental whole-animal genotypes. Local attribution to microglia is supported by CR3 expression and absence of other CR3-positive cells in the inspected P5 dLGN; the manipulation is not a microglia-restricted inducible knockout.

CTB-positive volume inside reconstructed microglia, projection overlap and juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta are distinct anatomical observables. They do not directly measure synaptic efficacy or prove one exclusive sequence of activity, complement tagging and engulfment.

Engulfment is reduced, not abolished, in CR3/C3 knockouts. Complement-independent and nonphagocytic mechanisms remain possible. Raw images, complete supplementary methods and the updated supplementary document remain unread; sex is not established by the selected main methods.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher identity and listed comment checked. Bachas, Physical Review D 23, 1037-1041 (1981), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1037, concerns an approximate instanton cutoff interpretation, not replacement Monte Carlo data or an erratum to the loop fits. The original Reference 1 swaps the Gross-Wilczek and Politzer page numbers; use their original DOI identities. contexts.finding: The fitted area coefficients show a crossover near beta=2 and a decrease compatible with the leading SU(2) asymptotic-freedom slope under fixed-string-tension renormalization. This is evidence within the finite pure-gauge model.
limitations: The paper studies a statistical lattice ensemble, not detector events or the real-time formation of a flux tube.
At beta=3, the size comparison tests square loops through side six; side five is the largest used in the subsequent analysis. The main beta=2.1-3 data use a 10^4 lattice; other beta values use 8^4.
Figure 3 error bars are standard deviations of fluctuations over five iterations after equilibration, not a documented autocorrelation-corrected uncertainty of independent samples.
Hot/cold convergence and finite-size comparisons are diagnostics within the reported runs; no deposited configuration stream or independent Monte Carlo replay is admitted.
Fit square-loop expectations with W(S)=exp[-(A+B S+C S^2)] by minimizing mean squared deviations of loop values; identify C=a^2 K only within this fit model.
Below beta=2.1 only sides one and two are significant and the fit includes side zero; below beta=1.6 only side one is significant and area dominance is assumed.
The paper displays fit variants at beta=1.6-1.8 and 2.2/2.25. Above beta=2.5 the area term is too small relative to the perimeter term for an accurate tension determination.
Finite volume, available loop sizes, sampling and fit assumptions limit the inference. The fit is not a direct detector measurement or an independently reproduced asymptotic potential.
Use the fitted a^2 K in a renormalization prescription that holds K fixed; compare with the leading SU(2) form proportional to exp(-6 pi^2 beta/11).

Figure 6 uses an arbitrarily chosen normalization for the weak-coupling comparison. Equation 5.4 estimates Lambda approximately sqrt(K)/200 with uncertainty of roughly a factor of two in that coefficient.
The renormalization prescription is based on confinement and the loop fits have restricted resolving power; the comparison is conditional support, not an independent proof of continuum confinement.
The model contains no dynamical quarks. Its lattice bare coupling and scale normalization cannot be identified with CMS alpha_s, physical QCD string tension or a universal confinement threshold.
The crossover does not identify instantons or any other unique microscopic confinement mechanism; no real-time hadronization or stable-complexity rule is measured.
